title: Love Bombing
description: An intense, overwhelming shower of affection, gifts, flattery, and attention at the start of a relationship to create instant intimacy, dependency, and obligation.

sections.title: What It Is
sections.content: An intense, overwhelming shower of affection, gifts, flattery, and attention at the start of a relationship to create instant intimacy, dependency, and obligation—then used to control.

sections.title: How It Actually Appears
content: A new romantic partner says “I love you” within days or weeks, wants to spend every moment together, and buys expensive presents early.
A cult or extremist group greets recruits with euphoric acceptance, constant praise, and a ready-made community.
A boss heaps praise on a new hire, calling them “brilliant” and “irreplaceable,” then later exploits that emotional debt.

sections.title: Common Behaviors
content: Constant texting, calling, or messaging.
Declaring you’re soulmates far too early.
Grand romantic gestures disproportionate to the length of the relationship.
Rapid escalation: moving in together, sharing financial information, or making major commitments prematurely.

sections.title: Real Phrases
content: “I’ve never felt this way about anyone before.”
“We’re perfect together.”
“I can’t imagine my life without you.” (within weeks)
“You’re the most amazing person I’ve ever met.”

sections.title: Warning Signs
content: The pace feels overwhelming, but you’re told it’s a sign of passion.
You feel guilty for wanting space or time alone.
The affection feels addictive, but you sense something is off.
Any sign of pulling back triggers anger, tears, or guilt-tripping.

sections.title: Why It Works
sections.content: It hijacks the brain’s reward system (dopamine spikes) and creates a strong emotional bond (trauma bonding precursor). Reciprocity pressure: after receiving so much, you feel obligated to give back—including compliance, loyalty, and silence later.

sections.title: Protection Strategy
content: Delay major commitments until the euphoria fades and you’ve seen the person under stress.
Set small boundaries early and watch how they react. A healthy person respects limits; a manipulator punishes them.
Keep a journal: if you notice the relationship went from 0 to 100 in days, slow it down intentionally.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
content: Confusing love bombing with genuine passion. The difference is the intent to control that follows.
Believing you’re the exception and that this time it’s “true love” despite the speed.

sections.title: Real Scenario
sections.content: A woman meets a man online. Within a week, he sends flowers to her office, texts her good morning and good night daily, and tells her she’s “the one.” She feels swept off her feet. After two months, he begins isolating her from friends, demanding all her time, and becoming verbally abusive when she resists. The love bomb is now a cage.

sections.title: Key Insight
sections.content: Real connection grows slowly. If it arrives fully formed in a week, it’s not love—it’s a strategy.
